text: Can be installed as a managed, read-only bundle that stays current as the author ships, so you subscribe instead of forking
quote: subscribe to the set as a read-only, always-current bundle you don't edit, rather than a fork you own

text: Installer writes editable skill files into your project as ordinary files you own and can modify
quote: It writes the skills into your repo as ordinary files you own and can edit. Nothing updates behind your back

text: Install only the skills and agents you choose, then invoke them with a slash command
quote: Pick the skills and agents you use. The installer writes editable files into your project.

text: Nothing updates behind your back; you pull the latest changes explicitly with npx skills update
quote: Nothing updates behind your back; pull my latest changes when you want them with `npx skills update`.

text: One-line install via npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills, with an update command
quote: npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills Update with npx skills update

text: Listed in Claude Code's official plugin marketplace, installable with a single claude plugins install command
quote: `mattpocock-skills` was accepted into **Claude Code's official marketplace**... `claude plugins install mattpocock-skills` is now the documented route

text: Claude Code plugin install updates itself by default
quote: claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official ... Updates itself by default.

text: Installable as a Codex plugin via its marketplace, updating itself at startup
quote: codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ... Updates itself at startup.

text: Installable as a GitHub Copilot plugin via marketplace commands
quote: copilot plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills copilot plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock

text: Works with any agent, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Copilot
quote: Works with any agent Claude Code · Cursor · Codex · Copilot · 25 skills · MIT

text: Skill collection is released under the MIT license
quote: Works with any agent Claude Code · Cursor · Codex · Copilot · 27 skills · MIT

text: Skills are small, adaptable, composable and work with any model
quote: These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model.

text: Keeps the user in control of the process instead of owning it like GSD, BMAD or Spec-Kit
quote: Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control

text: Setup skill scaffolds per-repo config: issue tracker, triage label vocabulary and domain doc layout; run once before other skills
quote: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

text: Setup asks which issue tracker to use: GitHub, Linear, or local markdown files
quote: Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, Linear, or local files)

text: Alignment skills help you agree with the agent and think through a change before starting work
quote: They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them _every_ time you want to make a change.

text: Grilling skill interviews the user relentlessly about a plan and maps it as a design tree until shared understanding
quote: Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**

text: grill-with-docs builds a shared language with the AI and records hard-to-explain decisions as ADRs
quote: This is built into [`/grill-with-docs`]... It's a grilling session, but that helps you build a shared language with the AI, and document hard-to-explain decisions in ADR's.

text: Asks the full set of open questions in one round, numbered, each with a recommended answer
quote: Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer.

text: Dispatches a sub-agent to look up environment facts (filesystem, tools) needed to answer design questions
quote: When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it

text: CONTEXT.md document helps agents decode the project's jargon
quote: It's a document that helps agents decode the jargon used in the project.

text: TDD skill drives a red-green-refactor loop: write a failing test first, then only enough code to pass
quote: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

text: Tests are written only at seams written down and confirmed with the user beforehand
quote: Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam.

text: Tests verify behavior through public interfaces rather than implementation details
quote: Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details.

text: Works in vertical slices: one test, one implementation, repeat, each as a tracer bullet
quote: Work in vertical slices instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a tracer bullet

text: Reads GLOSSARY.md and ADRs so test names and interfaces match the project's domain language
quote: read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs

text: Triage skill moves issues and external PRs through a state machine: categorise, verify, grill, write agent-ready briefs
quote: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

text: Treats a PR as an issue with attached code, using the same triage roles, states and machine
quote: a PR is an issue with attached code, using the same roles, same states, and same machine

text: Verifies a reported claim before triage, e.g. reproducing a bug from the reporter's steps
quote: Verify the claim. Before any grilling, check that the claim holds up. For a bug, reproduce it from the reporter's steps.

text: Labels issues as ready-for-agent (fully specified for AFK agents) or ready-for-human
quote: `ready-for-agent`: fully specified, ready for an AFK agent - `ready-for-human`: needs human implementation

text: Turns an agreed conversation into a written spec
quote: Turn an agreed conversation into a written spec.

text: Splits a spec into small tickets an agent can build
quote: Split a spec into small tickets an agent can build.

text: Builds a finished spec into code, test-first
quote: Build a finished spec into code, test-first.

text: Reviews a diff against your standards and against the spec
quote: Review a diff against your standards and against the spec.

text: Charts a large effort as a map of decisions and settles them
quote: Chart a large effort as a map of decisions, and settle them.

text: Answers a design question with throwaway prototype code
quote: Answer a design question with code you then delete.

text: Produces cited answers researched from primary sources
quote: Get a cited answer, read from primary sources.

text: Finds modules worth refactoring and presents them as a visual report
quote: Find the modules worth refactoring, as a visual report.

text: Diagnoses hard bugs starting from a failing reproduction
quote: Diagnose a hard bug, starting from a repro that fails.

text: Resolves merge or rebase conflicts hunk by hunk
quote: Finish a merge or rebase conflict, hunk by hunk.

text: Generates a script that walks a human through setup
quote: Generate a script that walks a human through setup.

text: Writes up a long session as a handoff so another agent can continue it
quote: Write up a long session so another agent can continue it.

text: Helper skill tells you which skill to use for your current situation
quote: Find out which skill to use for the situation you are in.
